| 7 | 9 | `if EEG.srate > 250` | ✅ exact | Condition. |
| 8 | 10 | `EEG = pop_resample(EEG, 250)` | ✅ exact | Same anti-aliasing filter, padding and ratio as EEGLAB's pop_resample (see the eeglab_resample() helper at the top of the script).<br>Matches EEGLAB when MATLAB's Signal Processing Toolbox is installed (EEGLAB then uses resample()); without it EEGLAB falls back to spline interpolation.<br>EEGLAB resamples each segment between 'boundary' events separately; this resamples continuously, so results differ near boundaries. |
| 9 | 12 | `EEG = pop_eegfiltnew(EEG, 'locutoff', 0.1, 'hicutoff', 30)` | ✅ exact | Same filter as EEGLAB: transition band, filter length, Hamming window, cutoffs and edge padding all follow pop_eegfiltnew/firfilt. Filter coefficients are identical; validated against EEGLAB output (see README).<br>Filtering restarts at 'boundary' events, as EEGLAB's firfilt does. |
| 10 | 13 | `EEG = pop_reref(EEG, [])` | ✅ exact | Average reference reduces data rank by one. If ICA follows, set n_components to at most (number of channels - 1). |
| 11 | 14 | `EEG = pop_epoch(EEG, {'S  1' 'S  2'}, [-0.2 0.8])` | ✅ exact | Same samples as EEGLAB: limits are rounded the way epoch.m does and the final sample is excluded, so epochs have EEGLAB's length (e.g. [-1 2] s at 128 Hz gives 384 samples, not MNE's 385).<br>baseline=None because pop_epoch does not baseline-correct; pop_rmbase does.<br>Events are placed at floor(latency) as EEGLAB does, which matters after resampling when latencies fall between samples. |
| 12 | 15 | `EEG = pop_rmbase(EEG, [-200 0])` | ✅ exact | EEGLAB gives the baseline in milliseconds ([-200, 0]); MNE uses seconds. |
| 13 | 16 | `EEG = pop_saveset(EEG, 'filename', sprintf('%s_epo.set', subjects{s})…` | ✅ exact | Saved as .fif (MNE native). Exporting back to .set needs the eeglabio package. |
